messages:
mohammed: Hey team — quick Q. I was a contractor until Feb and switched to FT on Mar 15. My last 1099 ended Feb, current benefits kicked Mar 15, but I got billed by my previous COBRA admin for March premiums. Do I need to elect COBRA for that gap or can benefits be backdated? Any payroll/benefits coordination I should do?

sophia (People Ops): @mohammed sorry for the hassle — short answer: usually coverage can't be retroactively backdated before your FT effective date, but we can coordinate with payroll + the COBRA vendor to avoid double-pay. Can you DM me the COBRA notice PDF? :mailbox_with_mail:

people-ops-bot: For benefit portal and vendor contacts see: https://benefits.redwood.example/portal (TPA: AcmeBenefits, COBRA inbox: cobra@acmebenefits.example)

ben (Benefits): Hi Mohammed — two things: 1) If you had continuous coverage under the contractor plan and the contractor plan was separate, COBRA might apply for the contractor period. 2) If your FT enrollment was processed on 3/15 and payroll deducted premiums on 3/20, coverage effective 3/15 should be billed to FT payroll. If Acme already invoiced you for the month, we normally ask them to void or credit that invoice once they confirm FT enrollment.

jake (Payroll): @mohammed to add context from payroll side: our cutoff for retroactive premium changes is the pay period close BEFORE the pay date. If your enrollment paperwork reached benefits before the Mar 10 payroll close, we could've adjusted Mar 20 deductions. Since it arrived after, we can do two things: 1) request Acme to refund/credit; or 2) process a one-time adjustment in the next payroll to offset double-charge (requires proof from Acme). I can initiate the payroll adjustment once benefits confirms vendor credit.

mohammed: Got it — thanks. I filed enrollment on Mar 16 via the portal (saw confirmation email). I can share the Acme invoice now. If Acme won't refund, is there a standard payroll code you use for the one-time offset?

sophia (People Ops): Thx. Send the invoice to people-ops@redwood.example and CC payroll. For the payroll offset we use code: "BEN-OFFSET-ONE" — include the vendor invoice number and date. Example instruction we send to payroll:
```
Subject: Payroll offset request — Mohammed — Acme invoice 2023-00345
Body: Please apply a one-time pre-tax payroll credit to employee Mohammed (employee ID 14321) equal to $XXX for month of Mar to offset COBRA charge. Attached: Acme invoice and benefits confirmation.
```

ben (Benefits): Also for dependent claims during the gap: if the claim date is between end-of-contractor coverage and FT effective date, it's governed by the contractor plan/COBRA. If Acme denies coordination, submit an appeal to Acme with the FT enrollment confirmation and we can help escalate. Add me on the appeal email (ben@redwood.example).

mohammed: Perfect. I emailed the invoice and CC'd payroll + @sophia. One last Q — will this affect my HSA payroll contributions setup? I had HSA elections on contractor platform before FT and set up pre-tax deductions now too.

jake (Payroll): If you keep HSA as pre-tax through payroll, we should align contributions with the FT plan going forward. If Acme collected HSA before FT, those are separate (they shouldn't have unless contractor plan offered HSA). If a correction is needed we can file an adjustment to contributions; that process can take one pay cycle.

sophia (People Ops): Great — we'll triage: 1) benefits confirms FT effective date and sends vendor note to Acme; 2) Acme asked to void/credit invoice; 3) payroll will apply BEN-OFFSET-ONE if needed and confirm HSA alignment. Will update once I have Acme's response. :white_check_mark:

mohammed: Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:
